questions.q: Per the book, pseudo-strabismus refers to:
opts: An apparent deviation of the eyes
A true latent deviation shown only on cover test
A manifest deviation constant in all gazes
questions.exp: Pseudo-strabismus: apparent deviation — the eyes only appear to deviate without true misalignment. (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: the book divides pseudo-strabismus into two types — pseudoeso (apparent convergent squint) and ______.
questions.exp: Types of pseudo-strabismus: pseudoeso and pseudoexo. (Book p66)

questions.q: Which statement about telecanthus (the first cause in the book's pseudoeso list) is FALSE?
opts: It shows an increased inter-canthal distance
It produces an apparent convergent squint
It is a cause of apparent outward squint
questions.exp: Telecanthus: ↑ICD + normal IPD — it is a cause of PSEUDOESO (apparent convergent squint), not pseudoexo. (Book p66)

questions.q: Match the telecanthus measurement with its status in the book — 1) ICD (inter-canthal distance) 2) IPD (inter-pupillary distance) … A) Increased B) Normal
questions.exp: Telecanthus: ↑ ICD + normal IPD — the two distances are dissociated. (Book p66)

questions.q: A 5-year-old appears to have a convergent squint. Measurement shows an increased inner canthal distance with a normal inter-pupillary distance and no true ocular deviation. Per the book this appearance is:
questions.exp: Pseudoeso due to telecanthus: ↑ICD + normal IPD produces an apparent convergent squint. (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: per the book, epicanthus is an extra (congenital) fold of skin connecting the ______ to the ______ in the medial part.
questions.exp: Epicanthus: an extra (congenital) fold of skin connecting the upper eyelid to the lower eyelid in the medial part. (Book p66)

questions.q: All of the following are listed causes of pseudoeso (apparent convergent squint) in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Pseudoeso causes: telecanthus, epicanthus, myopia. ROP causes PSEUDOEXO (via temporal displacement of the macula). (Book p66)

questions.q: Per the book, hypertelorism (the first cause of pseudoexo) shows an increased inter-canthal distance because of:
questions.exp: Hypertelorism: increased ICD — d/t wide-set orbits; causes apparent outward squint (pseudoexo). (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: in the book's list of pseudoexo causes, ROP expands to ______.
questions.exp: ROP: retinopathy of prematurity — a cause of pseudoexo due to temporal displacement of the macula. (Book p66)

questions.q: A premature infant who developed retinal disease after birth now shows an outward-appearing deviation. Per the book, ROP produces pseudoexotropia by:
questions.exp: ROP → pseudoexo: d/t temporal displacement of the macula. (Book p66)

questions.q: Which statement about pseudoexotropia (apparent outward squint) is FALSE per the book?
opts: Hypertelorism shows an increased ICD due to wide-set orbits
ROP acts by temporal displacement of the macula
Hypermetropia is one of its listed causes
Myopia is one of its listed causes
questions.exp: Pseudoexo causes: hypertelorism, ROP, hypermetropia. Myopia causes PSEUDOESO. (Book p66)

questions.q: Match the type of pseudo-strabismus with its third listed cause — 1) Pseudoeso 2) Pseudoexo … A) Myopia B) Hypermetropia
questions.exp: Pseudoeso causes: telecanthus, epicanthus, myopia; pseudoexo causes: hypertelorism, ROP, hypermetropia. (Book p66)

questions.q: Per the book, myasthenia gravis is most commonly seen in:
questions.exp: Myasthenia gravis: m/c in young females. (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: the pathology of myasthenia gravis per the book is ______.
opts: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
questions.exp: Pathology of myasthenia gravis: reduced Ach (acetylcholine) receptors. (Book p66)

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman has bilateral ptosis and double vision that are barely present on waking but clearly worsen by evening and improve with rest. Per the book the diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Myasthenia gravis: m/c in young females; fatigue worsens in the evening — the m/c feature. (Book p66)

questions.q: Which statement about myasthenia gravis is FALSE per the book?
opts: It is m/c in young females
Its pathology is reduced Ach receptors
Fatigue, worsening in the evening, is its m/c feature
questions.exp: Ptosis — bilateral — is a hallmark ocular feature, so the eyelids are very much affected. (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: the ptosis described in the book's ocular features of myasthenia gravis is:
questions.exp: Ocular features of MG: a. Ptosis — B/L. (Book p66)

questions.q: Per the book, Cogan lid twitch sign is:
opts: An upward twitch of the eyelid when changing gaze from down to up
A downward twitch when changing gaze from up to down
Retraction of the globe on adduction
Twitching of the brow on exposure to light
questions.exp: Cogan lid twitch sign: upward twitch of eyelid when changing gaze from down to up. (Book p66)

questions.q: Fill up: per the book, orbicularis oculi weakness in myasthenia gravis is tested by ______.
opts: Forced closure of the open eyelids
questions.exp: Orbicularis oculi weakness: tested by forced opening of closed eyelids. (Book p66)

questions.q: Match the ocular feature of myasthenia gravis with its description — 1) Ptosis 2) Diplopia 3) Cogan lid twitch 4) Orbicularis oculi weakness … A) Bilateral B) Double vision C) Upward twitch of eyelid when changing gaze from down to up D) Tested by forced opening of closed eyelids
questions.exp: Ocular features: ptosis — B/L; diplopia; Cogan lid twitch — upward twitch on down-to-up gaze change; orbicularis oculi weakness — tested by forced opening of closed eyelids. (Book p66)

questions.q: All of the following are ocular features of myasthenia gravis per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: MG ocular features: ptosis (B/L), diplopia, Cogan lid twitch sign, orbicularis oculi weakness — pupillary involvement is not one of them. (Book p66)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Per the book, the drug injected for the Tensilon test of myasthenia gravis is:
questions.exp: Tensilon test: injection of edrophonium. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Per the book, the Tensilon test uses an intravenous injection of ______ of edrophonium.
questions.exp: Tensilon test: Inj 0.5 mg of edrophonium. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Fill up: edrophonium in the Tensilon test is an ______ agent, and it ______ the acetylcholine.
questions.exp: Edrophonium is an anticholinesterase agent → ↑ Ach. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: A patient with suspected ocular myasthenia receives the Tensilon injection. Per the book, a positive test shows, after injection:
questions.exp: Tensilon test flow: before injection → after injection → improvement of ptosis. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Per the book, in the ice-pack test the ice pack is applied over the eye for:
questions.exp: Ice-pack test: ice pack application for 5 mins. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Fill up: a positive ice-pack test per the book shows ______.
questions.exp: Ice-pack test: application for 5 minutes → ptosis improvement. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Which statement about diagnosing myasthenia gravis is FALSE per the book?
opts: Edrophonium raises acetylcholine at the junction
The ice pack is applied for 5 minutes
In the book's Tensilon test, neostigmine is the injected drug
questions.exp: The Tensilon test injects edrophonium (an anticholinesterase agent → ↑Ach), not neostigmine. (Book p67)

questions.sec: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon and ice-pack tests
questions.q: Match the diagnostic test with its description — 1) Tensilon test 2) Ice-pack test … A) Injection of edrophonium → ↑Ach → improvement of ptosis B) Application over the eye for 5 minutes → improvement of ptosis
questions.exp: Diagnosis: Tensilon test (edrophonium → ↑Ach → ptosis improvement); ice-pack test (5 minutes → ptosis improvement). (Book p67)

units.title: Pseudo-strabismus — apparent deviation, its two types and causes
units.guide: Pseudo-strabismus = apparent deviation. Two types: pseudoeso (apparent convergent squint) and pseudoexo (apparent outward squint). Pseudoeso causes: 1. Telecanthus — ↑ICD + normal IPD; 2. Epicanthus — an extra (congenital) fold of skin connecting the upper eyelid to the lower eyelid in the medial part; 3. Myopia. Pseudoexo causes: 1. Hypertelorism — increased ICD d/t wide-set orbits; 2. ROP (retinopathy of prematurity) — d/t temporal displacement of the macula; 3. Hypermetropia.

units.title: Ocular myopathies — Myasthenia gravis: pathology, fatigue and ocular features
units.guide: Ocular myopathies — Myasthenia gravis: m/c in young females. Pathology: reduced Ach receptors. Fatigue: worsens in the evening (m/c feature). Ocular features: a. Ptosis — B/L; b. Diplopia; c. Cogan lid twitch sign — upward twitch of eyelid when changing gaze from down to up; d. Orbicularis oculi weakness — tested by forced opening of closed eyelids.

units.title: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis — Tensilon test and ice-pack test
units.guide: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis: 1. Tensilon test — Inj 0.5 mg of edrophonium (an anticholinesterase agent) → ↑Ach; before injection → after injection → improvement of ptosis. 2. Ice-pack test — ice pack application for 5 mins → ptosis improvement.
